children.value: Machine learning seeks useful structure in data and predictors that remain accurate on new observations. We begin with dimensionality reduction and clustering, then develop regression and classification through empirical risk minimization, regularization, and kernel methods. Connections with inverse problems explain the role of model assumptions, while the final analysis of generalization balances approximation error against the statistical complexity of the chosen model class.

Imaging problems often concern the reconstruction or processing of an individual signal or image, whereas machine learning studies patterns across collections of observations. Their goals and performance measures differ, but both use tools such as linear models, regularization, and convex optimization.
